messages:
maya: Heads-up — after last night's KMS rewrap there are sporadic 403s for embeddings routes. Throwing to eng-security to triage.

maya: Symptoms: embeddings requests from a handful of customers started failing with 403 scope errors while chat/generation calls kept working. Error in nginx logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden - scope_mismatch
route: /v1/embeddings
api_key_id: sk_live_...
allowed_scopes: [\"chat:write\"]
requested_scope: embeddings:vector_create
```

sam: I see a cluster of these in the audit logs around 2026-03-19T23:40Z — rotation job completed ~23:36Z. deploy-bot shows the rewrap finished at 23:35:41Z.

deploy-bot: rewrap-job/rotation-2026-03-19 succeeded (job id r-20260319-04) :white_check_mark:

leo: Quick hypothesis — KMS rewrap path rewrites the key metadata tags (we attach allowed_scopes to wrapped blobs). Maybe the rewrap code truncates or mangles the allowlist array for some tokens, leaving only chat scope.

maya: That's what audit trace implies: the KMS metadata for affected tokens shows allowed_scopes="chat:write" after rewrap; pre-rotation it was ["chat:write","embeddings:vector_create"].

sam: Repro steps I ran on staging: 1) create API key with scopes chat+embeddings; 2) run the rewrap job; 3) call embeddings => 403. Logs show the wrapped-key metadata post-wrap contains a single string instead of array.
```
pre-wrap: {"allowed_scopes": ["chat:write","embeddings:vector_create"]}
post-wrap: {"allowed_scopes": "chat:write"}
```

leo: That matches. Looks like a serialization bug in the rotate lambda when writing tags to the new wrapped object. The KMS client library call expects tags as map<string,string> and we flatten arrays to comma-separated strings in one code path.

ir-lead: Impact: medium — only tokens that hit the rewrap path during that window are affected. We have a small list of customer API keys in the audit events. Action plan: contain, patch, and remediate.

maya: Immediate mitigation options: (A) disable permissive scope fall-through so any token with missing or malformed allowed_scopes is rejected (safer) — but that could break a few other legacy keys; (B) re-run rewrap with fixed serialization to fix metadata for impacted tokens; (C) craft a hotfix in auth service to treat comma-separated allowed_scopes as list (back-compat).

sam: I'd prefer (C) short-term + (B) long-term. C is fastest (minutes) and allows us to restore embeddings for affected customers quickly. Then run B to correct metadata, and rotate again with validated tags.

leo: Patch idea for auth service (pseudo): 
```
allowed = metadata.get('allowed_scopes')
if isinstance(allowed, str):
    allowed = allowed.split(',')  # back-compat for malformed tags
```

maya: Fine. Sam — can you push a tiny patch to auth-service to accept comma list and deploy to canary? Add a strict-validate flag behind a feature flag so we can toggle.

sam: On it. I'll push branch sam/fix/scope-compat and cut a canary deployment to auth-canary cluster. ETA 20m.

deploy-bot: deploy auth-service sam/fix/scope-compat to auth-canary started by @sam

leo: Also proposing we add a nightly integration test exercising the full rotate+metadata roundtrip (create key -> wrap -> read metadata -> assert same scopes). Catches regressions.

ir-lead: Agreed. For remediation steps: 1) apply auth fallback patch (C) to reduce customer impact; 2) run targeted rewrap (B) for affected keys with correct serialization; 3) invalidate/tokens if customer requests. I'll prepare customer comms draft after we confirm scope restoration.

maya: I'll compile a short affected-keys list from audit and ping support for prioritized outreach. Please annotate each key with pre/post metadata and whether rewrap fixed it.

sam: Canary shows embeddings calls succeed for previously failing key after canary deploy. Rolling to prod in 10m if no regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy auth-service sam/fix/scope-compat to auth-prod started by @sam

maya: After prod patch and targeted rewrap, we should also add a strong unit test in the rotation job that fails if tags change shape. Also file a follow-up to remove the temporary back-compat later (tracked as SEC-4532).

leo: I'll open PR for the rotation-job serialization guard and the nightly integration test.

ir-lead: Good triage. Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (serialization mismatch when writing KMS tags), blast radius (list of keys), mitigation steps, customer impact and comms, and follow-ups (tests + remove fallback). Assigning owners: sam -> prod patch & rewrap; leo -> rotation-job fix + tests; maya -> customer comms + audit evidence.

maya: Thanks team. I'll start the comms template and add the keys to the incident doc. Will update thread with customer list once I have it. :thumbsup:
